title: Attach an installable extension ZIP to the public release
evidence: GitHub latest release 1.0.0 has zero uploaded assets. The two displayed downloads are GitHub source archives. The README and website tell users to download justpractice-*.zip and load an extracted manifest.json, which is not available there.
impact: A recruiter or new user following the primary download path cannot install the advertised build without installing development tools.
action: Publish the verified runtime ZIP as a release asset, add concise release notes, and point the download CTA directly to that asset. Keep source archives clearly separate.
accept: In a clean profile, download the release asset, extract it, load unpacked, and finish onboarding without npm. Verify manifest.json is at the archive root.

title: Reject unrelated or invalid backups before clearing data
evidence: The UI accepted {"unrelated":"not a JustPractice backup"}. After the existing confirmation, chrome.storage.local contained only that unrelated object; the library and settings were removed. The handler validates only that the root is an object.
impact: Selecting the wrong JSON file can erase a user’s library and practice history. There is no validation preview or automatic recovery copy.
action: Require a recognizable JustPractice payload and supported schema, validate nested values and size, show a restore summary, and retain a recovery snapshot until replacement succeeds.
accept: Reject empty/unrelated/malformed/oversized backups without writing. Valid exports round-trip. A failed write after clear restores the previous snapshot.

title: Keep the expanded watch panel inside short browser windows
evidence: At a settled 1280×600 viewport, the panel bounds were x=949, y=-127, width=300, height=639. Its drag/collapse controls were above the viewport; Playwright could not click collapse because it was off-screen. Default positioning uses bottom:88px and skips the clamp for auto top/left.
impact: Users in a short window can lose access to the controls needed to recover or move the panel.
action: Constrain panel height to available viewport space, keep the drag bar visible, make the body scroll, and clamp default as well as saved positions after content/layout changes.
accept: At 1280×600, 1024×600, and 200% zoom, drag/collapse/save remain reachable. Resize, collapse, expand, and popup reset preserve valid bounds.

title: Make the focus setting affect the playback meter
evidence: The checkbox persists and changes hint text, but practiceMeterEligibility passes no focus value or pauseWhenUnfocused flag. isEligibleForPlaybackMeter always checks only saved/enabled/visible/not-ended. The focus accessor has no call sites. The attempted two-window check could not establish a genuinely unfocused document under browser automation, so this conclusion is from the source.
impact: The setting promises a behavior difference that the meter does not implement.
action: Define whether focus means active tab or active browser window, then implement that policy in the meter; alternatively remove the ineffective setting and describe visible-tab counting accurately.
accept: Controlled tests distinguish visible/focused, visible/unfocused, and hidden playback with the option on and off. Document the same rules on every surface.

title: Align instructions with the current saving and counting behavior
evidence: README, popup help, dashboard empty state, and XP rules refer to a “Count practice time” toggle, but current panel markup has no such control: counting follows saved-library membership automatically. README also advertises a thumbnail hover strip that did not appear on the live search page, and README/manifest still advertise removed goal reminders.
impact: First-time users are asked to find controls that do not exist. The portfolio’s feature claims disagree with the product.
action: Choose the intended automatic/opt-in behavior, update all six locales plus README/site/manifest/tutorial, and remove retired strings and claims. Make save-to-start and pause behavior explicit.
accept: A new user can explain when counting starts/stops after reading only the UI. Each advertised interaction exists in the current release.

title: Raise contrast and size of essential helper text
evidence: axe measured the watch-calendar weekday labels at 3.28:1 (#666 on #111, 9px), below its 4.5:1 requirement for normal text. Onboarding subtitle text measured 2.97:1. Calendar legend and other very small labels are difficult to read in the captured panel.
impact: Core instructions and calendar context are hard to read, especially on lower-quality screens or for users with low vision.
action: Use shared readable muted-text tokens, increase small helper text, and verify text over translucent surfaces against real YouTube backgrounds. Keep subdued future states distinguishable.
accept: Scan extension-owned UI for contrast failures and manually verify visible text at 100% and 200% zoom. Exclude YouTube-owned findings from extension counts.

title: Repair onboarding roles and name the popup XP bar
evidence: axe found focusable progress buttons inside aria-hidden=true, buttons inside a role=listbox without option semantics, and a popup progressbar without an accessible name. These are extension-owned findings; unrelated YouTube ARIA errors are excluded.
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users receive inconsistent or missing information during setup and progress review.

accept: No violations for aria-hidden-focus, aria-required-children, or aria-progressbar-name. Complete onboarding and navigate core views using keyboard only, then perform a screen-reader check.

title: Apply Hebrew language and direction consistently
evidence: The dashboard correctly set lang=he and dir=rtl. The Hebrew popup retained lang=en with no dir, and Hebrew onboarding set lang=he but no document direction. The screenshots show left-to-right control layout mixed with Hebrew content.
impact: Reading order, punctuation, assistive pronunciation, and navigation layout vary between screens for the same language.
action: Centralize locale application for dashboard, popup, onboarding, and shadow panel. Use logical CSS properties and isolate Latin tags/numbers where necessary.
accept: Hebrew snapshots have correct document/shadow direction and language metadata; mixed Hebrew/English titles and numbers read correctly. Verify French, German, Spanish, and Japanese label lengths too.

title: Show save and failure feedback for user mutations
evidence: Several settings and library handlers await send() without checking an {ok:false} response. Export catches errors silently. Initial load has an error view, but successful/failed saves are not consistently acknowledged. Storage-quota and disconnected-worker errors were not fault-injected in this baseline.
impact: A user can believe a change was saved after the background rejected it, or receive no explanation when export fails.
action: Use one checked message helper; surface actionable inline errors and saved feedback; disable conflicting controls while writes are pending; preserve edited input on failure.
accept: Inject a storage quota failure and a rejected background response: the UI reports failure and retains the user’s input. Successful changes produce quiet, consistent feedback.
verification: 384 tests / 55 files, nine installed-browser scenarios, real service-worker quota rejection, rejected/disconnected messaging, export recovery, duplicate-write protection and draft retention passed locally. Six locale error layouts fit at 100%/200%, with scoped axe and measured contrast evidence. Unsaved drafts are in page memory; refreshing may discard them.

title: Give library removal an undo path
evidence: Clicking Remove deleted a card immediately; the library count changed from six to five. There was no undo affordance. Clear-all and restore already use confirmation dialogs.
impact: The most visually prominent action on each library card is destructive, and an accidental click loses the saved item and its metadata.
action: Move removal into a secondary action menu and offer an Undo toast. Keep explicit confirmation for full data replacement/clear rather than adding friction to every small action.
accept: An accidental removal can be reversed with its title, difficulty, completion status, and saved timestamp intact.
verification: Metadata-exact removal/undo, cross-view recovery and popup reopening pass; session/local-write failure, retry, stale membership, conflict, expiry and profile replacement are covered. Practice history and XP remain unchanged.

title: Make lint deterministic before and after building
evidence: npm run lint currently reports 106 errors and 25 warnings. Of these, 98 errors/16 warnings come from the generated public/assets/youtube-content.bundle.js; eight errors come from Node globals in build scripts. The earlier clean checkout had far fewer errors because the generated bundle did not exist.
impact: A basic quality command fails and its result changes after building, which weakens confidence for reviewers and CI.
action: Ignore generated public bundles and audit output; configure Node globals for scripts; remove unused source imports; decide how test files should be linted.
accept: On a clean checkout and again after npm run build, npm run lint succeeds with the same result and no generated-code findings.
verification: Local lint passes with zero errors/warnings before and after building; generated builds, release copies, browser reports and review artifacts are excluded.

title: Update and triage development-tool advisories
evidence: npm audit reports 20 affected packages: 8 moderate, 10 high, 2 critical. Critical entries are Vitest and Tinypool. npm audit --omit=dev reports zero advisories. These counts describe the installed development graph, not proven vulnerabilities in the shipped extension.
impact: The toolchain needs maintenance before inviting others to run it; severity needs context rather than a blanket claim that users’ browsing is exposed.
action: Update compatible toolchain versions, review remaining advisory conditions, rebuild and run the tests, and document any justified exception. Avoid an unreviewed force update.
accept: Known advisories are resolved or individually triaged with affected execution paths; test/build/package remain green.
verification: Critical/high advisories resolved. Raw audit retains seven moderate entries for one development-only Minimatch advisory, narrowly triaged with a 2027-02-09 expiry. Production audit reports zero findings.

title: Add a reproducible CI and release check
evidence: No .github workflow files are present. The project has meaningful unit tests and runtime-closure verification, but checks currently depend on a developer running them locally. TypeScript excludes test files from its build check.
impact: A future change can break installation or tests without an automatic signal on GitHub.

accept: A pull request gets a green, repeatable check and a runtime ZIP artifact. Add a separate test type-check if tests remain excluded from the app tsconfig.

title: Quote Windows archive paths
evidence: The Windows packaging command concatenates -Path and -DestinationPath values with spaces, without quoting them. Packaging succeeded in this workspace, whose path has no spaces; a path such as C:\Users\User Name\Projects will be parsed incorrectly. A spaced-path run was not performed.
impact: Another developer can build successfully but fail to produce the release ZIP on a common Windows folder layout.
action: Pass paths as literal, safely quoted PowerShell arguments or use a cross-platform archive library/tool with structured arguments.
accept: Package successfully from a workspace containing spaces and Unicode characters, and verify the resulting archive’s root manifest.
verification: Actual Windows packaging from spaces, apostrophe, Hebrew and bracketed paths passes: all 24 runtime files and manifest.json at root.

title: Make library cards easier to scan and act on
evidence: Titles are drawn over thumbnails that already contain text, while truncated channel names and red Remove buttons occupy the footer. A user can open the video by clicking the media, but the explicit action emphasis is removal.

accept: Long Japanese, Hebrew, and English titles remain readable, thumbnails are not obscured, and the main action is obvious at a glance.

title: Turn the repository into a clear project case study
evidence: The README explains installation and features but has no embedded screenshots, architecture overview, test command/results, design tradeoffs, known limitations, or maintainer-oriented contribution path. Several internal slimdown/audit documents are stale snapshots.

action: Lead with the user problem and a current screenshot/GIF; include a verified install path, concise architecture, local-data design, storage-race solution, checks, limitations, and a short roadmap. Archive or refresh stale audits; keep the tests.
accept: In under two minutes a reviewer can understand the problem, see the product, run it, locate the tests, and discuss one meaningful engineering decision.
verification: README leads with learner problem and current synthetic screenshots, architecture/storage-race decision, install/checks/limitations and roadmap. Contributor guide and historical-document labels make current instructions explicit.

title: Measure large-library and content-script costs before optimizing
evidence: The packaged ZIP is 284,940 bytes across 24 runtime files. The standalone YouTube script is roughly 627 KB uncompressed and has no minification option; it includes locale/UI code. The dashboard builds multiple view sections, including hidden ones. No representative long-session or 100+ video performance trace was taken.
impact: There are plausible startup/repaint costs, but current evidence does not justify claiming a performance defect.
action: Profile startup, search, playback sampling/calendar updates, large libraries, and memory over a long YouTube session. Then consider minification, selective rendering, and reducing unnecessary DOM replacement where measurements support it.
accept: Retain before/after traces and choose budgets for time to usable panel, search latency, long tasks, and memory. No optimization should regress tracking or packaging.
verification: 411 unit tests / 58 files and 18 installed-browser cases pass locally and on Linux/Windows. Final 25/100/500-item startup/search fits chosen budgets. The 346,144-byte watch bundle is 50.8% smaller; the 24-file ZIP is 17.4% smaller. Corrected controlled playback saved and displayed 598 seconds over 600 seconds. Final fixed-1080p60 normal-Chrome repeat passed: 609.099 seconds media over 647.903 seconds (94.0%, above the unchanged 85% threshold), with 603 practice seconds added. One final tick settled; the paused total then stayed stable and returned exactly on reload. Details focused Level. Earlier incomplete runs, a stall without JustPractice, panel-overlap setup notes and limits remain separately recorded; no universal speedup or zero-overhead claim is made.
